subject: Regional data stewardship questions after demo
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Singh <aisha@carebridgehealth.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@carebridgehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regional data stewardship questions after demo

Hi Aisha / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and helpful context on your ingestion patterns and expected TPS for tokenized transcripts. Quick recap and the follow-ups we agreed on: 

Summary of our call (short):
- Scope: patient-facing chat + clinician notes ingestion (PII/PHI concern called out).
- Residency ask: primary data residency in the US, but you want options for EU-only storage for a subset of customers later.
- Logs/retention: compliance team asked about access logs, audit retention, and whether logs can be turned off for certain flows.
- Failover/backups: you want assurance that cross-region failover doesn’t cause accidental cross-border data movement for pinned datasets.

Quick answers from the demo:
- PII handling: model inputs can be configured to avoid persistent KV caching; any cached prefixes can be disabled or encrypted per-tenant. We support customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption.
- Retention controls: per-account retention policies configurable (default 90 days). We can propose a 7-year archival pathway if required — archival is opt-in and can be limited to specific buckets.
- Logging & audit: request-level metadata (routing, timestamps) is stored in audit logs. We offer a “minimal logs” mode that removes user payloads but preserves telemetry for billing/uptime.
- Region pinning and failover: pin by account/caregiver cohort to a specific region (country-level). Cross-region failover works via warm-standby replicas; when failover occurs we keep pinned datasets local where required and route non-pinned traffic to fallback regions.

Open clarification items I promised to follow up on (please confirm):
1) For your PHI/PII definition: are patient identifiers (MRN, SSN) required to be stored in-region always, or can derivative embeddings be stored cross-region?
2) Retention target: you mentioned 7 years for clinical records — confirm whether 7 years must apply to all raw transcripts or only to records tied to closed cases.
3) Audit & access: who on your side needs access to audit logs (names/roles) and do you need log export to your SIEM?

Next steps we propose:
- I’ll share the residency whitepaper, SOC2 summary, and the demo recording (attached).
- Security deep-dive: suggest 60-min session with Karthik (infra), Monica (security) + your compliance lead. Proposed slots: Tue 2027-05-11 10:00 PT / Wed 2027-05-12 09:00 PT / Wed 2027-05-12 15:00 PT — please pick one.
- We’ll prepare a short diagram showing the failover flow that maintains country-bound datasets and a draft DPA snippet for your legal team.

Attachments included: redwood-residency-whitepaper.pdf, soc2-summary.pdf, demo-recording-20270509.mp4

Thanks — happy to handle anything else ahead of the security call.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@carebridgehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Aisha Singh <aisha@carebridgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Regional data stewardship questions after demo

Thanks Sergio — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our end: 

1) PHI scope: any direct patient identifiers (MRN, full name, SSN) must remain in-region (US) at all times. Derived embeddings may be stored outside the US only if they are one-way and not reversible; we will need a short technical note explaining how you prevent reconstruction.

2) Retention: our clinical retention policy is 7 years for active case transcripts; however, we will consider 90 days for ephemeral chat transcripts if you can show separation (i.e., ephemeral logs vs canonical records).

3) Failover: we need an architecture diagram that shows how pinned accounts are kept in-region during failover. Specifically: what happens to in-flight requests when a region becomes unreachable and we failover traffic? Does any customer data transit a foreign region in that window?

4) Dedicated capacity quote: please include a ballpark for dedicated capacity sized for ~50 concurrent users with 99.9% availability and a 15-minute RTO target.

5) Legal: we need your standard DPA + data processing additions for healthcare customers.

Can we aim to have the architecture diagram and DPA draft before the security deep-dive? That will make the call more productive.

Tom
Tom Reynolds
Director of Compliance, CareBridge Health
